notes.text: Sergio de Larrea and Tarik Biberovic are "both making progress, rehab's going well, and that's it," Dusty May said at Dallas practice. He gave no timeline for Dereck Lively II: "we're always going to err on the cautious side just to protect him and us."

Yanic Konan Niederhauser got into foul trouble in his return from a long absence for the Clippers. "Him getting used to it, getting in better shape, understanding timing," Tyronn Lue said. "It's going to take some time, you know, for him to get back to himself."

With Ja Morant and Deni Avdija out, Damian Lillard said after Portland's win over Milwaukee: "When you're down your next 2 top scorers... I knew that I would just need to be a little more assertive, a little more aggressive, and have more responsibility in that way. And I did."

Anthony Edwards cheered from the Timberwolves' bench in the loss to the Knicks. "It's just good to see him off the crutches, good to see him walking, and it's good to hear his voice during the games," Jaden McDaniels said.

Jonathan Kuminga played through a sore shoulder in the Timberwolves' loss to the Knicks. "I just had to test it out. You know, I could deal with a little pain, you know. And just going out there, it was still hurting."

Asked Thursday if he had retired from dunking, the Spurs' Victor Wembanyama said, "I did not, but if I can avoid it, I'll avoid it." He said a blister "definitely came from dunking a lot" and "every time I dunk, it kills me."

Donovan Clingan and Robert Williams are out. "What we want to be able to do is be able to sustain where we're at," Micah Nori said after Portland's win in Milwaukee. On Yang Hansen's 12 minutes: "We actually needed his minutes and it was good."

"Myles and Kuz dealing with just some things that flagged in the last game. You know, anticipate them just day to day. They should be back on Saturday," Taylor Jenkins said of Myles Turner and Kyle Kuzma after the Bucks' loss to Portland.

Jerami Grant will have imaging on his injured calf Friday. "No, no indication yet on the severity," Grizzlies coach Tuomas Iisalo said Thursday. "The good news is that it's the calf that's injured and nothing else."

Dylan Harper will miss time, Mitch Johnson said Thursday, calling it the best case after his fall but giving no timeline. The Spurs will have to "think a little differently than maybe we have so far this year in terms of lineups, rotations, different combinations."

Donte DiVincenzo is shooting on the court as he rehabs, Anthony Edwards said at shootaround. "Donte's on the court like shooting around," Edwards said. "I think he surpassed his rehab. Like, he's doing phenomenal."

Isaiah Joe returned after missing 10 games. "I know it's hard playing just those spot minutes sometimes to catch a rhythm," J.B. Bickerstaff said after the Pistons' game at New Orleans. He said the Pistons will "continue to bump his minutes up" as Joe progresses.

Nuggets coach David Adelman said he ran Aaron Gordon longer than usual in the win over Boston: "Sometimes we have to scrap what the minute thing is, not the restriction as far as how high it goes, but let him roll a little bit."

"The shot creation that is required from him... takes its toll," JJ Redick said of Luka Doncic with Austin Reaves out against Utah. Asked about Walker Kessler's slow start back from a one-game absence: "It's not Walker, it's not Luka... nobody had like a great game."

Darko Rajakovic said the injuries have made it "very, very hard" after the Raptors' loss to Washington. On rookie Allen Graves, who played 32 minutes and matched up with Anthony Davis: "Those minutes are super valuable."

Asked about coach Kenny Atkinson's 15-game evaluation after the loss to Memphis, Cleveland's Jarrett Allen pointed to absences, starting with Evan Mobley: "I think we have an identity and the base, but we just had so many circumstances that don't let us build upon it."

"Yeah, I was surprised. Yeah, I was surprised," Anfernee Simons said of learning about 30 minutes before tip at Orlando that Tyrese Maxey was out and he'd start for the 76ers. "Just be aggressive when it's there. Made the right plays, let the game come to me."

Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown were out for the 76ers' win at Orlando. Of rookie Labaron Philon Jr., LeBron James said: "He came in and gave us some big-time minutes, hit some big-time shots, gave us another ball handler, you know, obviously with Reese being out and JB being out."

Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown and Dean Wade sat the 76ers' win at Orlando. Maxey had foot soreness. He went through shootaround, then "said he was a little sore," Nick Nurse said. "All three of those guys... were probably abundance of caution situations."

"This was kind of planned, 3 games in 4 nights, just being cautious with his return to play," Darko Rajakovic said of resting Scottie Barnes against Washington. R.J. Barrett was also out with hamstring tightness after the Knicks loss, with the team "doing further investigation."

Nikola Topic, before his first Thunder home game of the season, on his ramp-up: "Obviously it's not 100% right now. I hope that will be soon. But yeah, I'm just trying every day to get back where I was before, and that's pretty much it."

"I still feel fatigued... I play like 2 minutes, everything just shuts down. And then it's just building that back up," Devin Carter said. He lost about 10 pounds while sick, missed four weeks and said G League games are helping him get his wind back.

"I felt wonderful. Like I could have played again. Felt like AAU," Jaron Pierre Jr. said at shootaround about the day after Saturday's game. On his minutes: "I'm finding my way... getting that trust from my teammates and the coaching staff and the front office."

Asked after the Lakers' overtime win over Charlotte if it was the finger, Quentin Grimes said: "Yeah, I gotta dislocate all my fingers or something like that. I'm gonna keep playing like that for sure."
"He's under the weather too," Chris Finch said of Jaden McDaniels after the Timberwolves' win on the second night of a back-to-back. "So I was trying to give him breaks early in the game if I could."

"We're still 9-5 with a lot of this road trip left and a lot of our pieces getting ready to come back healthy," Micah Nori said after Portland's 106-105 loss in Minnesota. "Jayson Kent knew that he was going to get the start about 37, 40 minutes before the game."

Jaylen Brown on 76ers teammate Tacko Fall, postgame: "He's been hurt a little bit... we need some more tall people." Brown said he'd like to see Fall get an opportunity: "he just got to stay ready, keep working, keep building off the injury he had."

Spurs coach Mitch Johnson said Tobias Harris is "progressing well." On a return before Christmas: "For his sake, I hope so." He said they'll take it "very methodical" and "whenever he comes back, it'll be later than he wanted and later than he probably could."

Micah Peavy "is doing a great job, but he's a 2-way. And so he can only play 50 games," Thunder coach Mark Daigneault said. "And so like the other night, we give him an inactive night to save a day and then we turn around against Sac and we like throw him in the game."

"TJ back playing and getting up to his normal minutes is important for us," Rick Carlisle said at Indiana Pacers practice before hosting Houston. Kelly Oubre Jr. said McConnell is still "getting his wind back, finding the rhythm in the game."

Keegan Murray said he threw up before the Kings' loss to Oklahoma City and doesn't remember half the game. He said he's not quite 100% but practised. "I feel like I'm in a better spot now than I was," Murray said. Doug Christie said everybody practised.

With De'Aaron Fox out in Utah, the Spurs' Jordan McLaughlin said: "You get a guy like Fox out, but you got other guys that can step up and provide minutes no matter how many minutes you play, 2 minutes, 3 minutes." He takes "anywhere from 300 to 800 shots a day" on off days.

Asked about Dejounte Murray's trade request and absence from the team, Derik Queen said at practice: "This was my first time going through it, but I just leave it to the front office. Wish DJ the best, wish he was here."

Yves Missi is back from rehab, and Zion Williamson was glad to see it. "Big time. You know, he worked really hard during his rehab. So to see him back out there was, you know, I was happy for him just for that," Williamson said at Pelicans practice.

"No, same injury report as before," Jamahl Mosley said of Trey Murphy III at Pelicans practice. "We might try to look at doing some more movement stuff on the court, maybe contact" Wednesday, "but we'll see how that looks." Trendon Watford and Bryce McGowens did not practice.

Cooper Flagg, ill in Boston, told Dusty May that Tuesday was the first day he woke up feeling good. "He was good," May said of Flagg's practice. Max Christie and Santi Aldama "both were full go," May said ahead of the Golden State game.

"I was playing 39 minutes. 36, 39 minutes. That was not the plan. So we kind of scaled back a little bit," Joel Embiid said after the game. On the past two weeks: "it feels like normal. It feels like I could play, you know, back to back."

Ryan Dunn played through a thumb problem in the Suns' win at Denver. "Ryan played through the thumb, you know, easily could have taken the night off and rest that thumb for him to go out there," coach Jordan Ott said.

Terrence Shannon Jr. scored a career-high 34 points. Rudy Gobert said: "So really happy for him. You know, he had a couple of rough games and he had an injury too. So we need him and it's great to see him back 100%."

Julius Randle on the hard hit to his lip in Monday's loss to Philadelphia: "I'm fine. It feels terrible, to be honest. But I'm fine. It just— I went to trap him, and he turned, and he didn't see me. Just kind of collided, but I mean, it's fine."

"It was hip tightness at that point... Sit him down," Erik Spoelstra said of pulling Bam Adebayo at halftime of the Miami Heat's win over Houston. "But I don't think it's a long-term thing." Spoelstra said Adebayo will be re-evaluated Tuesday.

"Yeah, I think we're still kind of working through it a little bit, you know. Again, the schedule kind of dictates it," Nick Nurse said of using LeBron James and Joel Embiid on back-to-backs. He said the 76ers will have to play somewhat different styles on those nights.

Amen Thompson's late scratch in the Rockets' loss to Miami is not a long-term concern, Ime Udoka said: "He has tendonitis that he manages pretty well and takes care of it. Just had a flare-up last night. If not for the back-to-back, I'm sure he would have been able to play."

Nolan Traore sat from late in the third quarter to about five minutes left against Philadelphia. "These guys have some sort of restrictions, and obviously I'm not gonna tell you what the minutes are, but we're doing what's best for their bodies," Nets coach Jordi Fernandez said.

"Chris stepped up, especially with Neem out," Jayson Tatum said of Chris Cenac Jr. after the Celtics' loss to Orlando, which Neemias Queta missed. "We're not gonna hold his hand when we get out there. We expect him to make plays because we know what he's capable of."

Jayson Tatum bruised his hand in the Celtics' win the night before and played through it in Monday's loss to Orlando. "Yeah, I bruised my hand last night, so just tried to wrap it, keep the swelling down a little bit," he said postgame. He said the hand did not limit him.

Neemias Queta sat out Monday's loss to Orlando. "He makes us a different team," Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla said. On Mitchell Robinson: "I think he's playing a role that we need him to play. It's a bigs by committee."

"Like, you know what, let me get my 30 so I can chill during the fourth quarter, but I ain't 100% yet," Jayson Tatum said after the Celtics' 131-94 win over Dallas. Baylor Scheierman said he is curious what 100% looks like given how Tatum is playing.

Luka Doncic hurt his ankle late in the Lakers' 123-112 win at Milwaukee on 12 Nov. "I'm good. You know, obviously it's painful a little bit, but I'll be fine," he said. Collin Sexton also left early. "They were good," Walker Kessler said of both. "Happy we got the win. You know, happy to go home."

"He's making progress," Erik Spoelstra said Monday of Pelle Larsson, out again with an illness. Larsson gets "a real good workout" today, and "we'll see how he responds tomorrow." On Myron Gardner's energy in his place: "That's who he is to his core."

Bones Hyland said at Timberwolves shootaround before facing Portland that the team will miss Jaylen Clark "for a little bit." "We're gonna, you know, hold it down for him and all the guys that's injured... he meant a lot to us, but it won't be for long."

"It's a couple of guys that have worked incredibly hard that are going to be knocked out for a long period of time," Thunder coach Mark Daigneault said. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander on the young players: "We're going to need them, and we're going to need the best version of them."

Ajay Mitchell returned for the Thunder after missing a couple of games. "He's obviously a high-impact player that can give us a lot of minutes and he helps us on both ends of the floor," Mark Daigneault said. "So you add that back in, it's pretty significant for us."

Zach LaVine missed the Kings' loss to Oklahoma City with a late illness. "We walked through, had a plan, everything, and then all that just happens and you just got to scrap it and throw it out the window," Doug Christie said.

Steven Adams returned for the Rockets in 4-minute stints. "It's gonna take some time to get his wind back, but those 4-minute stints, even in those, you can see what he does for us," Ime Udoka said. Fred VanVleet was out.

Keaton Wagler on Yanic Konan Niederhauser after the Clippers beat Charlotte: "I'll see him every once in a while and be like, Man, when you coming back? And he'll be like, man, soon. He's like, it's going to be Lob City."

"Definitely felt it. I think his on-ball defense is something that stands out," Orlando coach Sean Sweeney said at practice of having Jalen Suggs back. "I think, you know, he would say, you know, he's got to continue to get a little bit of that rust off."

Zach Edey sat out the Grizzlies' win over Brooklyn as a precaution. "We're just being very cautious with him. Zach's a tough guy and went through his, his pregame slot and... we didn't feel like this was, was the right decision," Tuomas Iisalo said.

GG Jackson played a few minutes against Brooklyn and didn't return. "Unfortunately it looks like relatively serious foot injury," Tuomas Iisalo said. "He was catching a good stride... there will be some, some further testing, but so far it doesn't look very good."

Jazz rookie Darryn Peterson, who asked out of Friday's loss to Houston with a knee issue, said he will play Sunday. "It's fine. Just got the shootaround. Feeling good," he said. "So it just bothered me a little bit, but I'm fine." He said he doesn't know how it happened.

"It was a quad. And again, you know, we just want to make sure we're taking care of him," J.B. Bickerstaff said of Duncan Robinson after the Pistons' loss in Miami. Asked about Ron Holland's injury, he said: "Not yet. I haven't had a chance to talk to our medical staff yet."

Memphis beat Brooklyn without Zach Edey, Quinten Post, Jerami Grant and Ty Jerome. "I know without Zach ... without QP, without a couple guys, JG, Ty, you know, like we needed that rebounding," Cedric Coward said after another double-double.

Kris Dunn had a bandage on his head and came out in the second half with a headband in the 113-112 win over Oklahoma City. "Oh, he's good," Tyronn Lue said. Asked if it was just little nicks, Lue said: "Yeah, he's all right."

"He gets on me a little bit because he tells me he can play more minutes," Micah Nori said of Damian Lillard after Portland's 120-107 win over Sacramento. "He didn't play for 18 months, so he'll even tell you, just continuing to knock the rust off."

"When ... you have a player of the level of Ben Simmons and ... 2 days before we're getting ready for our first game, I just think that the energy, it took a big hit," Kings coach Doug Christie said after the loss to Portland. He said there are no excuses at 1-11.

Klay Thompson sat out Miami's win over Cleveland with an ankle he hurt in Utah. "I was very sore the next 48 hours, and the progress I've made these last 3 days have been really great, so I look forward to hopefully being in the lineup" against Detroit Saturday, he said.

Rick Carlisle said Friday the Pacers are "spacing his minutes strategically" as guard T.J. McConnell returns "from being out for a while." "I really admire the way he's handling it because we're playing him in short stints," Carlisle said.

With Stephen Curry out, Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg said: "I gotta be a lot, lot, a lot more aggressive. Definitely have to be more in the score-first mindset now. My mindset so far has been like, you know, just support with Steph."

Bulls coach Tiago Splitter called Caleb Wilson's upper-body injury "just bad luck, you know, freak injury." He said "you just gotta be patient and go from there." On Wilson traveling with the team: "I'm not sure this travel, uh, but after that probably yes."

Asked Friday about De'Aaron Fox and Devin Vassell for the home game against Golden State, Spurs coach Mitch Johnson gave the same answer for both: "Optimistic. We'll still go through pregame just to make sure, but yeah, in a good place."

"Q was able to do the live part of the Stay Ready game," Lakers coach JJ Redick said Friday of Quentin Grimes. On Cameron Carr and Adou Thiero, who have both missed time, Redick said: "Those guys need reps." He said Carr has dealt with wrist and oblique injuries.

Jalen Suggs said he's good to play vs. Milwaukee. Sean Sweeney said Suggs, Tristan da Silva and Jamal Cain are questionable after taking part in shootaround. Sweeney on da Silva's calf strain: "there's always concern. We want them to be healthy and feel ready to go."

"I felt good, you know, no issues when it comes to the maintenance of the injury or anything like that," Grant Williams said after his return at Phoenix. "You just want to play more, but that's how, you know, return from injury comes."

Immanuel Quickley played 28 minutes. Darko Rajakovic confirmed Toronto is being careful with his hamstring. With Scottie Barnes and Kawhi Leonard out, "everybody's playing outside of their positions, playing a lot more minutes than when we have full roster," Rajakovic said.
"Our defense. Goody got stops... It's good to have him back. He changed the game all the time." Collin Gillespie on Jordan Goodwin after the Suns pulled away late to beat Charlotte.

"I felt great. You know, I'm 100%. I feel amazing," Domantas Sabonis said, asked about not looking 100% in his last game. On his role: "We have Doug, we have front office. You know, I get to speak to them and just understand what is it that is required from me."

Maxime Raynaud is out, Doug Christie said, but the Kings didn't sign Mason Plumlee over an injury. It's about making sure "Scott upstairs and those guys, they do their due diligence," he said. On Darius Acuff Jr.: "We want to keep the minutes in something that's manageable."

Warriors' Will Richard is playing with a torn thumb in a splint. He said he'll need surgery after the season: "They said it's inevitable. So I mean, I'm going through it where as long as it's not affecting the ligament, which they said it wouldn't, I'll be able to play."

"Yeah, I kind of saw when he first grimaced when he did it, but yeah, we just got to figure out a way to keep it afloat while he's out," Draymond Green said of Stephen Curry's injury. Curry told the team at halftime he was okay, teammates said.

Asked after Wednesday's loss to Houston if Gui Santos's knee is still bothering him, Steve Kerr said: "Yeah, I agree. I don't think he's moving as well as he normally does, so it could be. But yeah, we'll keep on that."

With Chet Holmgren out, Isaiah Hartenstein and Aday Mara played heavy minutes together in the Thunder's loss Wednesday at Portland. Mark Daigneault on the pairing: "they played a lot of minutes tonight" and "that's probably not sustainable either."

Marcus Smart was ejected in Houston's win. Ime Udoka: "I didn't see it, but Marcus, I just talked to him. He said they got wrapped up and his elbow that he had hurt got bent up. And so he said something to him and Bassey said, what you gonna do? And he did it."

Jaime Jaquez Jr. on his move to the Bucks' bench: "Coach told me he felt like... we needed some help on the bench and he thought I could fit there." Tyler Herro said Jaquez and Ryan Rollins balance the bench, and with Myles Turner back, "that's a good second unit."

Tyler Herro was back for the Bucks in Wednesday's loss after a scary fall. He said the knee injury was "like a bone contusion" and that he took Tuesday off: "did around-the-clock treatment, and got right."

Immanuel Quickley returned from injury in Toronto's loss to Boston, and Darko Rajakovic praised his defense. Collin Murray-Boyles was back from illness; Rajakovic said he's "not himself." Ja'Kobe Walter said "our bodies are adapting pretty well" to heavier minutes.

Aaron Nesmith left Wednesday's win over Washington with tightness in the back of his knee. "The hope is that it's minor," Pacers coach Rick Carlisle said. "You know, it's likely he'll be listed day to day."

Dallas' Morez Johnson Jr. practiced Wednesday. Dusty May hedged at first, then cleared him for Thursday: "everybody that, uh, played the other night is good to go, plus Morez." P.J. Washington said Santi Aldama's return adds shooting, smarts and size.

Portland's Chris Youngblood was limping after a breakaway against the Thunder and will have his foot checked. "I don't know if when he went to go finish whether he stepped awkwardly," Micah Nori said. With them again Wednesday, Nori kept stints short to keep bodies fresh.

Jalen Green limped to the bench in the win. Suns coach Jordan Ott said he thinks Green is okay: "I didn't hear anything, any update there after the game." Jordan Goodwin returned from injury and hit six threes for 18 points off the bench.

Franz Wagner is "just taking on a lot of the playmaking load," Anthony Black said after Orlando's win at Sacramento. "It's a lot of just advantage creation," Black said. "He's doing a really good job getting to the paint."

Keegan Murray came off the bench again in the Kings' loss to Orlando. Coach Doug Christie said it isn't about trying something new with De'Andre Hunter: "trying to ease him back until, you know, he's, he's feeling good."

Anthony Black says he can play against Sacramento. At the Magic's shootaround, he traced his overtime cramping in the last game to a rolled ankle: his calves and the rest of his body were compensating. "I think everybody's a little beat up, but yeah, good enough to play."

Asked if Norman Powell plays Wednesday, Bulls coach Tiago Splitter wouldn't commit: "I don't know. He did practice for half of practice." Zach Collins is "getting better," he said, and everybody else practiced. "Slowly getting everybody back."

Brandon Williams has a hamstring injury and will get an MRI, Steve Kerr said after the Warriors' win over New Orleans. Kerr called it a big concern: "We'll see how bad it is." He said they have "a lot of guys banged up" and he tried to rest some players in the fourth quarter.

Without Morez Johnson Jr. in Monday's win over Indiana, Dallas lost second chances, Dusty May said, and Daniel Gafford's short night made it worse: "when Gaff plays less than 20 minutes, I mean, that's a big part of our offensive rebounding."

Tyrese Haliburton's absence and T.J. McConnell's limited minutes were among the road-trip challenges Rick Carlisle listed after Indiana's loss in Dallas. "No excuses," he said, but "2 of the 3 games on this trip, we competed the way we need to compete."

Naz Reid on the back he was grabbing at, and wearing a wrap on, in the Hornets' win over Cleveland: "Nothing crazy. It just stiffened up on me." Reid said it tightened while he was sitting during the game and that he should have gone on the bike.

Bilal Coulibaly missed the Wizards' loss to Detroit. AJ Dybantsa called him "probably, like, the best defender." Anthony Davis returned; Brian Keefe said he thought Davis missed one first-half shot. Dybantsa, off his minutes restriction: "it's something I've been waiting for."

Charles Lee wouldn't call Brandon Miller day-to-day after the Hornets' game against Cleveland, but said Miller is improving every day: "I don't want to say day to day... But like, I don't think it's going to be a long-term thing." Naz Reid and Grayson Allen will be evaluated.

Zion Williamson was out Monday against Golden State for rest. "No, just rest," Pelicans coach Jamahl Mosley said before the game. With Williamson and Trey Murphy III out, Mosley named Jeremiah Fears, Dejounte Murray, Herb Jones, Saddiq Bey and Karlo Matkovic as starters.

Ime Udoka said Steven Adams and Clint Capela are targeting Washington and Miami, and Oscar Tshiebwe is sick, "hopefully a one-game thing." He said Houston will play small, with Jabari Smith Jr., Marcus Smart and Jae'Sean Tate taking turns on Nikola Jokic.

Ja Morant and Shaedon Sharpe are out for Portland, and Robert Williams sits out back-to-backs. Trail Blazers coach Micah Nori said Yang Hansen "has shown himself to be good on nights when Rob's been out" and Chris Youngblood has filled in very well.

Desmond Bane, who said he'd been confined to his room away from the team, was back moving around at Magic practice. "I'm feeling better, you know, trying to get my energy back." Anthony Black (cramps) is day by day, Sean Sweeney said.

Hawks guard Dyson Daniels said Monday that Onyeka Okongwu took "a little hit in the throat" Saturday and "he'll be fine. He's got a little croaky voice." With Jalen Johnson out for "those games," Daniels said, Atlanta is "really small in the starting lineup."

Joan Beringer wore a mask for his broken nose for the first time in Minnesota's win. "He a warrior, bro," Bones Hyland said. Hyland said he wasn't hurt on a hard first-quarter foul: "I tried to get a little flag foul."

Domantas Sabonis was supposed to play in Sunday's loss to Miami. "He wasn't" there, Kings coach Doug Christie said, so Precious Achiuwa played center. With Maxime Raynaud also out, Keegan Murray said they need rebounds from anyone: "We're not the biggest team in the world."

Baba Miller played a lot of minutes in the Clippers' 139-123 win over New Orleans, with Brook Lopez in foul trouble and Isaiah Jackson out. Tyronn Lue said Miller got to the paint and switched on defense: "he's all-purpose... be able to do a little bit of everything."

Dallas' Dusty May started Caleb Martin for defense, especially on nights Kyrie Irving sits, "and we don't know exactly when those are going to be." May said the win over Brooklyn let him "replace some guys" with a game the next night: "less taxing mentally and physically."

Kyle Filipowski was back on the floor in Utah's loss to Minnesota. "It was good to see Flip back out there. I thought he had some nice minutes," Will Hardy said. Hardy called it a tough stretch with a lot of injuries: "We're struggling to get over the hump right now."

With Isaiah Jackson out against New Orleans, the Clippers were down to Brook Lopez and rookie Baba Miller at center. "We got nobody else left," Tyronn Lue said before the game. Miller would get "extended run," Lue said, praising his energy and speed but expecting mistakes.

Nic Claxton played on a minutes restriction in the Bulls' loss to Philadelphia, his first real game in about a month. Asked how long it lasts: "Oh, no, no, I have no idea." He said he needed the restriction because "I was a little tired," and his hamstring felt fine.

Deandre Ayton played seven first-half minutes and none after halftime in the Wizards' loss at Oklahoma City. Coach Brian Keefe: "Just a lower leg, a calf. Got hit in the calf. That's all I have for right now."

Onyeka Okongwu left the win over Brooklyn. Quin Snyder said there was an adjustment period, "not wondering if you're going to have him." Aaron Wiggins said with bigs like Jock Landale and Asa Newell out, "we have to fill in as a team, and it has to be as a collective."

Mikel Brown Jr. will sit Sunday at Dallas; the Nets are holding him out of back-to-backs. "I'll obviously let you know when he does," coach Jordi Fernandez said. He said Brown's "body is where we want it to be" and back-to-backs bring "more risk."

Asked about heavy minutes, Miles Bridges said at Suns shootaround: "I really don't be feeling like I'm in game shape until after like the third game. So now I'm right where I want to be." On today's game: "Stopping Kevin Durant. Well, really stopping everybody."

Alex Sarr didn't really practice or work out over the summer because of a foot injury and is working his way back, Wizards guard Trae Young said Friday. Young called AJ Dybantsa, who missed the start of the season, a future star: "Now he's playing and trying to get his rhythm."

Brayden Burries, asked after Friday's loss if he jammed his shooting hand: "Yeah. No, I'm good. I'm good." Pressed, the Bucks rookie said, "Yeah, I'm good." On handling 38 minutes, he said he tries to sleep more than eight hours, plus naps and ice on the road.

Morez Johnson Jr. says the shin is "going away" and he's "back to being bouncy." Dusty May said Johnson got out of shape missing practice but looks game-ready after the Mavericks beat Utah. Naji Marshall, back from illness, played longer spurts and wasn't tired late, May said.

Peyton Watson returned in the Cavaliers' win over the 76ers. Kenny Atkinson on what stood out: "Defense. Peyton Watson. Big difference." Atkinson praised Watson's defense on Maxey and said: "we got to make sure we're empowering him to bring the ball up."

Sam Merrill started Friday's win over the 76ers with Jarrett Allen out. "Yeah, it's bothering him," Kenny Atkinson said of Merrill's elbow. For Saturday, he said "we'll see." Atkinson said the Cavs "needed him out there to stabilize us."

Brandon Miller began limping in the second quarter of the loss to Boston and asked to come out. Charles Lee said the Hornets will evaluate him over the weekend and know more Monday. Lee called it a storm, adding: "I know we're on the verge of a breakthrough."

No target date for Brandon Ingram. The Clippers forward, recovering from heel surgery, said he's done some 3-on-3 and 5-on-5 and is "pretty close," but needs more 5-on-5 and to get comfortable jumping. "It's gonna take a little time, but I'll be ready soon."

Tyrese Haliburton and T.J. McConnell are out, and Kelly Oubre called Haliburton one of two "monumental pieces" Indiana must "Hold it down" for until they return. Oubre on playing Saturday against Denver: "Yes, sir." Pascal Siakam: "we started getting guys back already."

"No, I'm not all the way back yet, man. I still don't have my pop." Sacramento Kings guard Malik Monk said he looks slow and a second late on tape after sitting out the preseason and the season opener. He said it isn't limiting him.

DeMar DeRozan tried to shoot before Denver's win over Toronto, then "came back down and said he couldn't," Bryce Hopkins said. The rookie said J.J. Barea told him about 30 minutes before tip he'd play. "No 2-minute scouting report. I had to be locked in," Hopkins said.

Vit Krejci fractured his leg, "is what it sounds like," Micah Nori said after the win over Phoenix. He wasn't sure if it was leg or ankle and has no idea yet on surgery. He said Chris Youngblood will take those minutes and John Tonje or Jayson Kent will probably be called up.

Devin Booker went back in after Suns coach Jordan Ott made sure he was okay. Once the loss got out of hand, Ott said, "you got to save some for tomorrow" against rested Orlando in the first back-to-back. "We got to win the recovery battle right now," he said.

Suns coach Jordan Ott said missing the injured Mark Williams hurts the defense: "Mark's overall size deters rim attempts." He said the Suns now switch more, pulling their 5s off the rim. Defensive rebounding has surprised him: "I did think we would be bigger this year."

Adem Bona has neck soreness after a hit in the 76ers' win over Detroit. "He looks to be okay, but nothing official on that," Nick Nurse said. Joel Embiid hopes Dominick Barlow is "back soon." Tyrese Maxey said his right pinky has looked that way since last year: "I'm fine."

Cameron Johnson of the Denver Nuggets said he is fine after pulling up late in Monday's game. He said he figured it was a cramp and stood on the sideline the rest of the way to be safe: "hamstrings, they get a little tricky sometimes, but I'm fine."

"The circumstances aren't gonna change, you know, in the short term," Mark Daigneault said postgame of short-handed Oklahoma City, adding there will be no excuses. Bennett Stirtz, Aday Mara, Micah Peavy and Josh Dix are "getting an opportunity and they're delivering for us."

"We've been trying to reinvent ourselves since Anthony went down," Timberwolves coach Chris Finch said after the win. He wants LaMelo Ball "more aggressive" as a scorer and playmaker, and "he's done that." Late, Ball made "the right play after the right play," Finch said.

"I think he's playing through a lot of pain right now," Jazz coach Will Hardy said Wednesday of Lauri Markkanen. Hardy wouldn't commit to Markkanen's minutes at center: "Be a night-to-night thing." He said those lineups spread the court.

DeMar DeRozan was out for Denver's win over Toronto. On Aaron Gordon, David Adelman said: "we'd like to keep him at a threshold." Adelman said he ran Gordon longer in the first quarter with Jamal Murray and Nikola Jokic. On Murray: "Jamal's played a lot."

Without Jayson Tatum for the first time this season, then without Payton Pritchard after he went out in the second half, the Celtics beat Milwaukee. Derrick White said they had no real point guard and were "running lineups that we haven't really done before."

Jalen Brunson can play 36 to 38 minutes, Mike Brown said after the Knicks beat Chicago. Brown said tracking in two-minute stretches shows Brunson doesn't fade. Brown won't push him: "It's going to impact him, in my opinion, come playoff time."

Jarrett Allen will be looked at Thursday after a knee-to-knee collision in the Cavaliers' loss to the Thunder. "Too early to determine," Kenny Atkinson said. Tyrese Proctor, starting for his defense on Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, left with "a pretty good twist."

Isaiah Jackson will play for the Clippers: "He's good," Tyronn Lue said. Rui Hachimura and Derrick Jones Jr. are back. Lue said returning players are usually on minute limits, so he has to "juggle the times." He said the Clippers "need to cut some guys' minutes down."

Alex Caruso sat out Oklahoma City's win at Cleveland, but "he was in everybody's ear just talking like he always does," Micah Peavy said at shootaround. Peavy, who guarded Harden, Mitchell and Mobley, said: "I like to be that guy that coach can call on to guard those guys."

Steven Adams is out with no timeline. Ime Udoka said that takes away Houston's favored double-big lineup, which he likes with Adams over Alperen Sengun and Clint Capela, but "gives other guys opportunity." Oscar Tshiebwe is a center option "if need be without Clint."

Steve Kerr said Jimmy Butler "would be my second choice when he's back" on Warriors technical free throws when Stephen Curry is off the floor. Kerr said Brandin Podziemski, Al Horford and De'Anthony Melton each missed one before Yaxel Lendeborg made one.

Max Strus returned in Monday's loss to the Raptors. "It was fun to get back out there and compete," he said. Strus said the Clippers have no reason to panic: "it's growing pains. We'll be all right." On his sharpness: "I'll just keep taking it day by day."

Tyronn Lue started Kris Dunn to help Darius Garland bring the ball up, but Dunn wore down too in the loss to Toronto: "To have him play 30 minutes in the back-to-back, that's not really fit for KD." Should Garland (back tightness) get a game off? "No, we'll take a look at it."

Stephon Castle played through a migraine in the Spurs' last game, a random thing he said he has had a couple of times before. In the morning, "it was kind of bad, but as I came into the game, it got better," he said. Castle also said San Antonio is "still not at full strength."

With the Timberwolves "down some bodies," Chris Finch said he wants to get Jonathan Kuminga more chances to attack: "We'd be lost without him right now for sure." Ayo Dosunmu: "We short on guys right now." Kuminga had 10 rebounds and 4 blocks against Milwaukee.

Isaiah Stewart played a lot of minutes with Zach Edey in foul trouble, and Grizzlies coach Tuomas Iisalo said Memphis has to be smart with him moving forward. "Some of the guys played very heavy minutes," he said, so the next practice will be handled carefully.

Rick Carlisle thinks a bruised knee made Kelly Oubre Jr. a last-second scratch, leaving Indiana with six players. Braden Smith's cramp was "not a pulled muscle or a strain as far as I know," he said. He said all six have earned "at least the consideration for more minutes."

Coby White knew his minutes number before tip-off in his first game back for the Hornets, and he thinks he went past it. "Probably played a little more than I was supposed to, actually," White said after the 124-91 loss to Detroit. He played a little under 16 minutes.
No Jock Landale and no Kingston Flemings for the Atlanta Hawks on Nov. 2, coach Quin Snyder said after the game.

Peyton Watson sat out the Cavaliers' loss to the Thunder. Kenny Atkinson said they're being cautious: "I'd rather him get, you know, fully healthy, you know, rather than throwing him out there game 6, game 7." Jaylon Tyson was also out.

Adou Thiero has had live exposures and is the only Laker not healthy, JJ Redick said Nov. 2: "Hopefully by the end of the week he'll be available." Ziaire Williams, back from a foot issue, is "not like on a minutes restriction," Redick said.

Darius Garland, Gradey Dick, Kobe Sanders, Brook Lopez and Kris Dunn were the Clippers' tentative starters for Nov. 2 because "the guys in their position ahead of them are out," Brian Shaw said. Asked about Brandon Ingram, he had "no update": "He's progressing."

Julian Champagnie said he thinks Utah's Lauri Markkanen will play against San Antonio on Nov. 2: "I think Markkanen is playing." Champagnie said Markkanen's return would change Utah's offense and who it runs plays for compared with the last meeting.

Rudy Gobert is sitting for the Timberwolves but travelled with the team. At shootaround he said he does not expect to be out long: "I don't plan to be on the sideline too much... that's why I really wanted to travel and be there with the guys."

Steve Kerr said Gui Santos sat the second half because his knee was bothering him, and Santos will also sit Nov. 2. "We'll reevaluate here over the next few days." The Warriors were already without Stephen Curry, Draymond Green, Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody.

Rookie Cameron Carr was available for his Lakers debut on Nov. 1 after a preseason injury, but coach JJ Redick would not commit to minutes or say whether he would play. "If he gets an opportunity... hopefully he shoots the ball well," Redick said.

Steven Adams and Reed Sheppard remain out for Houston, and Ime Udoka liked the response: "it felt good to see other guys step into those roles and us not really miss a beat." Fred VanVleet is coming off surgery; "we knew we wouldn't play back-to-back," Udoka said postgame.

Two guards out, and Memphis didn't know who until late after a tiring road trip. Coach Tuomas Iisalo's fix: Javon Small, who had barely played in the first five games, ran the second unit, and Cam Spencer played point with 13 assists and 0 turnovers.

No LeBron James and no Joel Embiid for the Philadelphia 76ers on Oct. 31, and no reason was given postgame. VJ Edgecombe confirmed both sat out and said the team's approach doesn't change: "every game matters, regardless of who's playing, who's not playing."

Ja Morant is out, and Micah Nori says Portland will miss him on turnovers. He wants more from Scoot Henderson, attacking the rim, not settling for pull-ups: "we don't need him to orchestrate everything for everybody else, just for him to go."

Oso Ighodaro is back with the Phoenix Suns, and after the Oct. 30 loss Collin Gillespie said the offense flows easier with him: "you could kind of just give him the ball and he's like a point forward. And he's a really good connector."

"I know he's 2 for 9, but it's his first game back. I love that he shot 9." Denver coach David Adelman on Cameron Johnson's return. Spencer Jones is "hopefully coming back soon," he said, with no firm timeline. Alpha Diallo and Julian Strawther will return "at some point."

Karl-Anthony Towns played Philadelphia with his wrist wrapped and said the injury predates it: "in the Bulls game for sure. That was when I did it." Asked if the wrist needs managing, no status was given: "that's something we'll deal with in the future."

"All available," Taylor Jenkins said of the Milwaukee Bucks. Kel'el Ware at center "has actually progressed to being something good for us," he said, though he wants more rim defense. Ware with Myles Turner? "At some point in the season. How soon, I can't predict."
